title: Govinda

teacherSummary.text: Old Govinda, still searching, comes to the ferry and asks for teaching. Siddhartha says that wisdom cannot be communicated in words, that every truth's opposite is also true, and that one must love the world. Asked to kiss Siddhartha's forehead, Govinda sees in his face a stream of countless faces and forms—the unity of all things—and bows, weeping, before his friend's smile.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Searching means: having a goal. But finding means: being free, being open, having no goal” slowly and put it in my own words: Siddhartha tells Govinda that searching means having a goal, while finding means being free, open and goalless. Next, craft. I notice the contrast between "searching" and "finding," explained like definitions. The strongest word is “free”: it shows that letting go of the goal, not chasing it, brings wisdom. Then, effect. What does Siddhartha teach Govinda about searching and finding? My answer: Govinda has searched all his life without finding peace because he is too fixed on the goal; Siddhartha teaches that openness, not effort, allows wisdom to come.
